title: A bioinformatics pipeline for processing and analysis of whole transcriptome sequence data
author: Ayam Gupta
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.brz8m79w
materials:
Equipment
1. Computer
Ideal configuration: 32/64 GB RAM with 64 core CPUs in an Ubuntu operating system (16.04.4 LTS
machine)
Software
All the softwares were downloaded from the following locations:
1. FastQC https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/FastQC
2. Bowtie2 https://bowtie-bio.sourceforge.net/Bowtie2
3. HISAT2 https://github.com/infphilo/Hisat2
4. Samtools http://samtools.sourceforge.net
5. Cufflinks https://github.com/cole-trapnell-lab/cufflinks
6. DeSeq2 https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/DESeq2.html
7. FeatureCounts-apt-get install featurecounts
8. 1000 genomes dataset: http://www.internationalgenome.org/
Dataset Information
For benchmarking, we have downloaded publicly available 1000 genome datasets
(http://www.internationalgenome.org/) with three different population accessions, viz. East Asian (ERR1050076
and ERR1050078), American (HG00731 and HG00733) and African ancestry (NA19238 and NA19240)
(Table1). Each population contains an individual as parent and child and type of RNA sequencing is strand
specific using Illumina platform. The files were downloaded either using FTP link or fasterq-dump
(https://www.internationalgenome.org/data-portal/sample) [5].

steps.title: Prepare computational environment
steps.instruction: Use an Ubuntu 16.04.4 LTS machine with at least 16 GB RAM (64 GB RAM and 64 cores recommended) and create a shell script (extension .sh) to hold all commands.

steps.title: Run quality check with FastQC
steps.instruction: Execute FastQC on each raw FASTQ file to generate quality reports.

steps.title: Build genome indices
steps.instruction: Create Bowtie2 and HISAT2 indices for the human hg38 reference genome.

steps.title: Align reads to reference
steps.instruction: Map paired‑end (or single‑end) reads to the indexed hg38 genome using HISAT2 or Bowtie2, directing output to a SAM file.

substeps.instruction: # For single‑end data, omit the -2 option and use -U instead.

steps.title: Convert SAM to BAM
steps.instruction: Convert the SAM alignment file to BAM format with samtools.

steps.title: Sort BAM file
steps.instruction: Sort the BAM file to prepare for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Index sorted BAM
steps.instruction: Create an index for the sorted BAM file to enable rapid random access.

steps.title: Assemble transcripts with Cufflinks
steps.instruction: Run Cufflinks on the sorted BAM to assemble transcripts and estimate their abundances.

steps.title: Merge assemblies with cuffmerge
steps.instruction: Combine assemblies from all replicates using cuffmerge, providing the reference GTF and FASTA.

steps.title: Identify DEGs with Cuffdiff
steps.instruction: Perform differential expression analysis with Cuffdiff using the merged transcript GTF and the sorted BAM files.

steps.title: Generate read counts with featureCounts
steps.instruction: Count reads per gene using featureCounts to enable downstream DESeq2 analysis.
